details.description: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B is Alibaba's Qwen team's vision-language Mixture-of-Experts model, with about 235 billion total parameters (roughly 22 billion active), described by Qwen as "the most powerful vision-language model in the Qwen series to date." It launched September 23, 2025 and is listed by AWS as an Active model on Amazon Bedrock, where it accepts text and image input with a 256K-token context window. Its architecture adds Interleaved-MRoPE positional embeddings and DeepStack multi-level Vision Transformer feature fusion for visual grounding.
advantages: Supports OCR in 32 languages, up from 19 in the prior Qwen VL generation, with improved handling of rare characters and jargon (Hugging Face model card).
Documented visual agent capability: recognizes on-screen elements and invokes tools to operate PC and mobile GUIs (Hugging Face model card).
Can generate Draw.io, HTML, CSS and JS code directly from images or videos of interfaces or diagrams (Hugging Face model card).
Includes advanced 2D and 3D spatial grounding for visual reasoning tasks (Hugging Face model card).
Broader pretraining aimed at recognizing celebrities, anime, products, landmarks, and flora/fauna in images (Hugging Face model card).
disadvantages: On Amazon Bedrock this model's input modalities are limited to text and image; Bedrock's model card lists no support for audio, video or speech input or output.

Qwen's own release materials describe video understanding (hours-long video with second-level indexing), but AWS's Bedrock model card does not list video as a supported input modality for this deployment, so that capability could not be confirmed as available here.
use_cases: Document and OCR understanding across many languages
Visual agent workflows that operate GUIs by recognizing on-screen elements
Converting screenshots, mockups or diagrams into Draw.io, HTML, CSS or JS code
General multimodal question answering over images

sources.title: Qwen3 VL 235B A22B - Amazon Bedrock model card

notes: Both the Hugging Face model card and the GitHub README present their multimodal and text benchmark tables (MMMU, MMMU-Pro, MathVista, OCRBench, etc.) as embedded images rather than text, so no benchmark scores could be verified from the pages opened and evaluations is left empty; a numeric 'Real5-OmniDocBench Overall 88.9' score appeared in extracted text but its higher/lower-is-better convention could not be confirmed, so it was left out rather than guessed. OCR language support is stated only as a count (32 languages), so languages is left empty per instructions. Catalog facts (256000 max input tokens, 8000 max output tokens, image_input+text_input+text_output modality) match AWS's current Bedrock model card exactly.
